Generate Alt-Text for Data Visualisations

generate_alt_text.Rd

Generates alt-text for data visualisations using an OpenAI language model. The function accepts Quarto documents, R Markdown documents, and image files as input.

Usage

generate_alt_text(
  flnm = NULL,
  outfile = NULL,
  openai_model = "gpt-5.1",
  api = NULL,
  user_instruct = "",
  captions = NULL,
  combine = FALSE
)

Arguments

flnm

A character string or vector of character strings specifying the paths to input files or directories. Supported formats include Quarto (`.qmd`), R Markdown (`.rmd`), PNG (`.png`), and JPEG (`.jpg`, `.jpeg`). Directories are searched for supported files.

outfile

A character string specifying the path and file name of the output text file. Defaults to `"alt-text.txt"` in the current working directory.

openai_model

A character string specifying the OpenAI model used to generate alt-text. Defaults to `"gpt-5.1"`.

api

A character string containing the OpenAI API key used for authentication.

user_instruct

An optional character string containing additional instructions to customise the style or content of the generated alt-text. These instructions are appended to the default system prompt.

captions

An optional character string or named character vector containing reference captions for image inputs. A single caption is applied to all images. Alternatively, supply one caption per image, either in the same order as the input files or named using the corresponding file names, including their extensions. Not applicable to document inputs.

combine

A logical value indicating whether multiple image inputs should be treated as panels or views of a single figure and described together in one alt-text. Defaults to `FALSE`. Only applicable to image inputs.

Value

Invisibly returns `NULL`. The generated alt-text, reference captions, and token usage information are written to the file specified by `outfile`.

Details

For Quarto and R Markdown documents, the function extracts potential ggplot code chunks and uses the R code, BrailleR output, and relevant reference text to generate alt-text.

For image files, the function analyses the supplied image(s) and optionally incorporates user-provided captions as reference text. Multiple images can also be combined to generate a single description covering the figure as a whole.

The function supports two input workflows:

Quarto and R Markdown documents

Identifies potential ggplot-generating code chunks and retrieves their associated figure references. The function attempts to evaluate the extracted R code and generate a textual description using BrailleR. If BrailleR output is unavailable, the source code is provided to the language model instead.

Image files

Generates alt-text directly from image content, optionally incorporating reference captions. When `combine = TRUE`, multiple images are treated as panels or views of a single figure and described together.

Generated alt-text follows the default description guidelines, covering chart type, axes, approximate ranges, visual mappings, patterns, and relevant interpretations. A checklist is also included to indicate whether these elements have been addressed.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Generate alt-text from a Quarto document
generate_alt_text(
  flnm = "report.qmd",
  api = Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
)

# Generate alt-text from an image
generate_alt_text(
  flnm = "figures/plot.png",
  api = Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
)

# Generate alt-text with a reference caption
generate_alt_text(
  flnm = "figures/plot.png",
  captions = "Relationship between temperature and pressure.",
  api = Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
)

# Combine multiple images into a single description
generate_alt_text(
  flnm = c("figures/panel_a.png", "figures/panel_b.png"),
  captions = "Comparison of two distributions across different groups.",
  combine = TRUE,
  api = Sys.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")
)
} # }
